description: Tokenized Asset Purchase: submit a token’s transfer restrictions with its secondary venues and the buyer: the token with whether holders must be whitelisted, the date its lockup ends, who must approve a transfer (no one, the issuer, a transfer agent or the platform), the transfer fee, the jurisdictions barred from holding it and its wording, read for freely transferable, no restrictions or permissionless; each secondary venue with its name, kind (an exchange, an ATS, a DEX, OTC or the platform), whether it is open to the buyer and when it last traded the token; the holder with whether the buyer and the counterparty are whitelisted, the buyer’s jurisdiction and when the buyer may need to transfer; and the date transfers are read at. The signed report gives the restrictions with the wording found, every venue as trading, open, stale, closed or unread with the days since its last trade, and the holder, and counts them, and names a locked token: a lockup that runs past when the buyer may need to transfer, a whitelist the buyer or the counterparty is not on, a barred jurisdiction, no venue open to the buyer and free-transfer wording the restrictions contradict; then a transfer approval, a transfer fee, open venues with no trade in 30 days and a lockup that ends in time, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. An unstated whitelist rule, approval rule, venue list, transfer date, whitelisting, jurisdiction or reading date leaves transfers unverified. This reads one token’s transfer restrictions after purchase: two Atlas assets’ rights side by side are wever_atlas-compare and a consent grant’s onward rule is wever_consent-transfer-check. Verdict tokenized_transfer_locked, tokenized_transfer_partial, tokenized_transfer_unverified or tokenized_transfer_free. POST /api/tokenized-transferability-check. Reads the purchase records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Tokenized Asset Purchase reads the buyer’s own records for one purchase of a tokenized asset and checks each step before money moves: the quote against its stated terms, the platform’s terms against the buyer, the custody arrangement, the redemption path, the transfer restrictions, the settlement, the claimed backing and the full cost. Beside it, wever_atlas-asset-passport and wever_atlas-redemption-check read what the published Tokenization Atlas dataset records about an asset by its id, while a purchase check reads the records the buyer supplies for one purchase; and wever_vendor-quote-check and wever_price-truth-check read quotes and charges for goods, services and paid calls, while the quote and cost checks read a token purchase against its own terms. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/tokenized-purchase-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/tokenized-asset-purchase/.

transfer_by.description: When the buyer may need to transfer, such as 2026-11-20.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

read_at.description: The date transfers are read at, such as 2026-11-20.

text.description: Read for wording such as freely transferable, no restrictions or permissionless.
